summary: Labels split into 12 ornithine HCl rows and 8 L-ornithine L-aspartate rows, which aren't one evidence set. The stored trial's fatigue result in all 17 people reads as a within-trial comparison; its placebo differences are in women only. Small trials at 400 to 1,600 mg show stress and mood changes, mostly without named primary outcomes. LOLA trials are in cirrhosis at 15 to 18 g a day against 3 g on the label, and Cochrane is very uncertain.
question_for_clinician: Can small stress and fatigue trials in healthy Japanese adults credit 500 to 1,000 mg ornithine HCl, and should cirrhosis LOLA data be kept off 3 g supplement labels? Agent recommendation: no credit to either; hepatic encephalopathy treatment is not a supplement purpose.
